findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
findings.body: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` was changed to subclass `StatefulDetectorHandler` with an empty body (`pass`). `StatefulDetectorHandler` declares four abstract members (`counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and the newly added `build_occurrence_and_event_data`), none of which are implemented here, so the class remains abstract under `ABCMeta`. `MetricAlertFire.detector_handler` still points at it, and `Detector.detector_handler` does `group_type.detector_handler(self)`, which will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler ...` for any `Detector` whose `type` is `metric_alert_fire` (which is also the default type produced by the `create_detector` test fixture). Previously this handler was a working no-op (`evaluate` returned `[]`); now `process_detectors` will crash instead of skipping. Either implement the abstract members (even as stubs) or leave the class as a concrete `DetectorHandler` until the real implementation lands.

findings.title: Expected occurrence built with wrong group key in TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe
findings.body: In `TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe` the expected occurrence is built with `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", 6, PriorityLevel.HIGH)`, which sets `fingerprint=handler.build_fingerprint("val1")` -> `["<id>:val1"]`. The code under test is then invoked with group key `"group_key"`, so the real hook produces `fingerprint=["<id>:group_key"]`. `IssueOccurrence` is a frozen dataclass with field-wise equality, so `DetectorEvaluationResult(...) == expected_result` will be False and the assertion on line 546-560 fails. The expected occurrence must be built with the same group key (`"group_key"`) that is passed to `evaluate_group_key_value`.

findings.title: Mock occurrence builder ignores `value`, so tests don't verify the value passed to the hook
findings.body: `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` accepts a `value` argument but never uses it, so the tests cannot detect whether `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate_group_key_value` passes the correct value into `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. This is already masking inconsistencies in the new tests: `test_results_on_change` evaluates `{"val1": 100}` but builds the expected occurrence with `value=6`, and `test_state_results_multi_group` evaluates `group_2` with `10` but builds the expected occurrence with `6`. Include `value` in the mock occurrence (e.g. in `evidence_data` or `subtitle`) so a regression in the argument passed to the hook would actually fail a test, and fix the mismatched values in those tests.

findings.title: evaluate() docstring still says it returns a list
findings.body: `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` was changed to return `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`, but its docstring still reads "returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`". Implementers reading the docstring will get the wrong contract; update it to describe the dict keyed by group key.

findings.title: Stale TODO comment about becoming a stateful detector
findings.body: The comment `# TODO: This will be a stateful detector when we build that abstraction` is now wrong: this PR makes `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` subclass `StatefulDetectorHandler`. The stale TODO should be removed or replaced with a note about the abstract methods that still need to be implemented.
